status_effects.explanation: Her skill at producing an intellectually crafted impression of frivolity is presented as a subtle mark of depth, mildly raising her local esteem.

He is marked by vulgar arrogance and a manner that once displeased the grandmother, contrasted unfavorably with Saint-Loup's grace, though partly offset by the narrator's concession of his genuine ancient-grandeur qualities.

appraisal_events.evidence: il avait fallu beaucoup de sérieux pour qu'elle donnât dans sa conversation et dans ses Mémoires le sentiment de la frivolité, lequel est intellectuel
appraisal_events.explanation: In an analogy used to explain Saint-Loup, the narrator credits Mme de Villeparisis with an underlying seriousness that makes her apparent frivolity in conversation and in her Mémoires an intellectual achievement rather than mere superficiality.

appraisal_events.evidence: eût décelé de morgue vulgaire, j'avais pu en prendre conscience ... chez le duc de Guermantes"; "dans l'ensemble commun qui avait tant déplu à ma grand'mère ... offrait des parties de grandeur ancienne
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator identifies vulgar arrogance in the duc de Guermantes's hereditary familiarity, unlike the graceful version he found in Saint-Loup, and recalls that his manner had once displeased the grandmother; yet the narrator concedes he also possessed genuine touches of ancient grandeur perceptible when dining with him.
